method: Uses the Cisco IOS auto-cost convention rather than presenting the formula as an OSPF standard: for each outgoing interface, divide the integer reference bandwidth in Mbps by the interface bandwidth in Mbps, truncate the positive quotient to an integer, and raise results below 1 to 1. Link bandwidth is parsed as a decimal with at most six places and converted to integer micro-Mbps, so truncation at exact integer boundaries does not depend on binary floating-point rounding. A calculated per-interface cost above 65535 is refused rather than clamped because it cannot be represented by the OSPFv2 router-LSA metric field. The path cost is the sum of the individual outgoing-interface costs and may exceed 65535. Results expose raw quotients, truncation, minimum-cost application, and cases where different speeds collapse to cost 1. One to 24 links are accepted; the reference bandwidth is an integer from 1 to 4294967 Mbps and link bandwidths are from 0.000001 to 4294967 Mbps. The RFC defines directional configurable costs, not this bandwidth-derived formula. Manually configured costs, vendor-specific behavior, actual interface bandwidth settings, and the reverse direction must be verified on the target routers. All processing is browser-local.
